label_descriptions.empty: An empty input array returns an empty array. The agent's tests should include at least one assertion exercising empty input.
label_descriptions.single: A single interval is returned unchanged (in a new array). The agent's tests should include at least one assertion exercising the single-interval case.
label_descriptions.non-overlapping: Disjoint, non-touching intervals remain separate in the output. The agent's tests should include at least one assertion where the input intervals do not overlap and the output keeps them separate.
label_descriptions.overlapping: Two or more overlapping intervals are merged into one spanning their combined range. The agent's tests should include at least one assertion exercising overlap merging.
label_descriptions.adjacent-touch: Two intervals that touch exactly (one ends where the next begins, e.g. [1,2] and [2,3]) are merged into [1,3]. The agent's tests should include at least one assertion exercising the adjacency/touching merge rule.
label_descriptions.unsorted-input: Input intervals may be given out of order; the output is always sorted ascending by start. The agent's tests should include at least one assertion where the input is not pre-sorted.
label_descriptions.contained: An interval fully contained within another is absorbed (e.g. [1,10] and [3,4] -> [1,10]). The agent's tests should include at least one assertion exercising full containment.
label_descriptions.point-interval: Zero-length point intervals (e.g. [5,5]) are valid and follow the same merge rules. The agent's tests should include at least one assertion exercising a point/zero-length interval.
